plan.hypothesis_assessment:
Partially supported. The baseline established that
the unchanged method can learn the task and that its late training improvement
corresponds to a 12-point gain in measured task success. It did not establish a
policy satisfying the human objective. The 0.89 training proxy versus 0.615
protected-task success is an important discrepancy; code inspection confirms
that training uses a radius-band curriculum while research evaluation uses the
official uniform radius range. This observation guides the next investigation
but does not by itself show that the distribution difference caused the gap.

partial_evaluations.label: late diagnostic: checkpoint-120832
partial_evaluations.selection: The protected task-reference result for this artifact is 61.5% (123/200), with 77 failures, while training proxies reached success_rate 0.89 and ep_rew_mean 169.5. Measuring the endpoint with researcher diagnostics is useful because the observed task deficit and truncation-only failures leave the reach-versus-hold composition uncertain; first reach, maximum held steps, interruptions, and geometry could change the next intervention choice and whether this checkpoint remains the working or best-known policy.

partial_evaluations.label: late diagnostic: checkpoint-115712
partial_evaluations.selection: This checkpoint measured 49.5% (99/200) on the same protected panel, and the endpoint comparison has 44 F-to-S versus 20 S-to-F transitions. Measuring its reach and hold diagnostics on the shared episode identities is useful for determining whether the endpoint's 12-point task gain corresponds to broader acquisition, more stable holding, or a mixed shift; that result could change the failure-mode target and the decision to keep the endpoint over this comparator for further development.
